newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians lose $10 million a day from closure.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians lose $10 million a day from closure.

text.p: Crippling Israeli travel restrictions imposed in the West Bank and Gaza Strip after last week's violence have raised daily Palestinian economic losses to about $10 million, trade officials said on Wednesday.

Samir Huleileh, deputy undersecretary of trade in the Palestinian Authority, said Israel had paralysed trade within the West Bank and between self-rule areas and the outside world, causing shortages of basic supplies.
"Movement between the Palestinian cities has been halted and imports and exports have also ground to a halt," Huleileh said. "We estimate our daily losses to be around $10 million."
Israel barred Palestinian movement between autonomous West Bank cities in the wake of last week's clashes, which claimed 57 Palestinian and 15 Israeli lives.
The Palestinian Ministry of Economy and Trade said in a statement that Palestinian losses had risen from $6 million daily before last week's violence to about $10 million now.
Even before the latest violence, Israel maintained a closure on the West Bank and Gaza Strip that restricted foreign trade and limited work permits for Palestinians seeking jobs in Israel.
"The latest Israeli measures come at a time when the Palestinian economy is already hard hit by the closures," the ministry said in a statement.
A spokesman for Israel's coordinator of affairs in the West Bank and Gaza expressed doubt about Palestinian figures but gave no estimate of his own.
"We have in past received economic estimates from the Palestinians but it is difficult to relate to them seriously because they change all the time and are unfounded," the spokesman said.
The Palestinian ministry said some areas in the northern West Bank had begun to suffer shortages of food, petrol and cooking gas. Farmers have been unable to deliver produce.

"Food is available...But there is a serious problem with gasoline," Nablus governor Mahmoud al-Alloul said. He told Reuters Israel had allowed some petrol to enter the city of 130,000 on Tuesday, but none on Wednesday.

Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip depend entirely on Israel for supplies. Israeli-PLO interim peace deals that began Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip give Israel control of international crossing points and internal roads in both areas.
"The Israeli army is now cutting off Palestinian cities, imposing curfews in the areas under its control and preventing basic commodities from getting to the shops," the ministry said.
The Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions said about 23,000 labourers with permits to work in Israel had been kept from their jobs for a week.
Inside the self-rule areas, some Palestinian factory owners said their businesses were working at 30 percent capacity as many workers were unable to reach work.
Issam al-Akkad, owner of one of the largest garment factories in the West Bank, said his plant could close within four days if he did not receive raw materials.
"The effect of what is happening is very, very dangerous," Huleileh said. "The travel ban will increase political and economic resentment in the areas."
